verdict.summary: Canaan is a distressed ASIC vendor with an attached self-mining operation, not a clean bitcoin proxy. Q1 revenue was $62.7 million, including $42.9 million of mining-machine product revenue and $19.1 million from mining, but gross loss was $22.9 million and GAAP net loss reached $88.7 million. The company produced 257 BTC and increased installed computing power to roughly 11 EH/s, yet negative gross profit shows that scale did not cover inventory, pricing and energy economics. July operations improved global operating hashrate to 14.24 EH/s and treasury to 1,917 BTC plus 3,952 ETH; Ethiopia was paused, so installed capacity overstates active output. The capital structure also matters: 63.66 million ADS were sold at $1.131 in November 2025, and the current 724.7 million share-equivalent snapshot leaves material dilution sensitivity. A D grade is appropriate before September 3 results. The event veto is absolute: neither the $0.45 reference activation nor valuation framing is actionable until fresh earnings reset the facts and geometry.

whyAvoid: Q1 gross loss was $22.9M on $62.7M revenue.
Canaan reported an $88.7M GAAP loss; adjusted EBITDA remained negative at $76.3M.
Only 46 BTC were mined in July despite 14.24 EH/s operating hashrate.
Ethiopia was paused, making installed capacity a poor output proxy.
63.66M ADS were sold at $1.131 in the November 2025 offering.

business.overview:
Canaan sells Avalon ASIC mining machines and operates its own bitcoin-mining fleet. Hardware revenue depends on machine shipments, selling price and inventory write-downs; mining revenue depends on active hashrate, BTC price, network difficulty and power cost. Q1 product revenue was $42.9M and mining revenue was $19.1M. Subsequent customer cash collections of $42M matter because receivable conversion supports working-capital reuse.

The AI transmission channel is semiconductor-adjacent rather than direct. Canaan designs specialized compute silicon, but Avalon chips solve SHA-256 mining workloads, not AI training or inference. AI foundry demand can instead compete for fabrication capacity and raise wafer or packaging costs without creating Canaan AI revenue.

The model breaks when ASIC prices fall below inventory cost, customers delay payment, deployed machines remain offline, or power and difficulty erase mining spread. ADR dilution, foreign-private-issuer disclosure cadence and the paused Ethiopia fleet add financing and operating uncertainty that treasury coins cannot remove.
business.moat: Canaan has long ASIC-design experience, an Avalon product brand and access to both machine sales and self-mining feedback. The moat is constrained by larger competitors, commoditized hash output, foundry dependence and customers' willingness to defer purchases when miner payback periods deteriorate.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Canaan's ADS structure requires per-ADS discipline. The October 24, 2025 424B5 created a new up-to-$270M ADS ATM, with each ADS representing 15 Class A shares; it also states that the terminated 2024 program had sold 21,088,579 ADS for about $42.5M net. The November 4 filing separately records 63,660,477 ADS sold at $1.131. The minimum observable basic denominator in the current market snapshot is 724.7M ADS equivalents. A current fully diluted ADS denominator is explicitly unavailable because the reviewed filings do not reconcile options and warrants; diluted per-ADS NAV is therefore not calculable.

filingsReview.summary: 6 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade D measures fundamentals; trade state rejected measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The May 19 6-K furnishes Q1 results showing $62.7M revenue, a $22.9M gross loss, an $88.7M GAAP net loss, 257 BTC produced and roughly 11 EH/s installed capacity; it is operating disclosure, not securities issuance.
The 2025 Form 20-F establishes foundry, inventory, customer-credit, China-linked regulatory and ADR risks plus the annual liquidity baseline; it is periodic disclosure rather than an equity issuance.
The August 17 6-K furnishes July operations showing 14.24 EH/s operating hashrate, 46 BTC mined, $0.043/kWh power cost and a paused Ethiopia fleet despite installed capacity.
The June EFFECT notice only confirms that a registration statement became effective; it contains no securities sold, proceeds received or dilution incurred and cannot be classified as issuance.
The November 4 prospectus records a primary sale of 63,660,477 ADS at $1.131, creating actual cash proceeds and dilution rather than merely preserving unused shelf or ATM capacity.

The October 24 prospectus establishes a new up-to-$270M at-the-market program for ADSs, each representing 15 Class A shares; it also reports 21,088,579 ADS sold for about $42.5M net under the terminated 2024 program. New capacity is not completed issuance.

contrarianRisks: The November 2025 424B5 records an actual ADS sale; the June 2026 EFFECT notice is registration effectiveness, not issuance.
Foreign-private-issuer reporting provides less frequent US-style quarterly detail.
Installed hashrate includes capacity that may be paused; operating hashrate and BTC output are the economic measures.
Negative gross profit means treasury value cannot be treated as surplus to a self-funding operation.
ASIC inventory can be impaired rapidly when bitcoin economics or chip generations change.

macro.impact: CAN is hit first by BTC miner payback periods and ASIC replacement demand, then by foundry pricing and China-linked supply or policy friction. AI chip demand can crowd fabrication capacity but does not create direct revenue because Avalon silicon is mining-specific.

risks.riskSummary: Canaan combines negative gross economics, weak liquidity, ADR dilution and volatile fleet utilization; the September 3 earnings event can invalidate every current operating and valuation inference. Retail war-room: the ADS can gap beyond the dated $0.455/$0.423 range on earnings or a China/crypto headline; thin liquidity means wider spread and severe slippage. Keep sizing at zero before the post-event rebuild and do not chase either boundary of the rejected map.
